local_checks.invariant: Every procfs, sysfs and os-release read must use a fixed path or a validated one, be size-bounded, close its descriptor, and not allow traversal or unbounded growth
local_checks.result: readSmall (util.go:42-49) opens the file, defers Close and reads through io.LimitReader, so each read is bounded and no descriptor leaks. All paths are constants, except the hwmon glob results and /sys/block/<name>. Names reaching /sys/block go through safeDevName (alnum, '-', '_', '!', '.', max 64) after a kernel-name prefix filter. A bare '.' or '..' would be accepted, but those names cannot come from /proc/diskstats, which the kernel controls, so there is no traversal. hwmon paths come from filepath.Glob on kernel-controlled sysfs. Mount paths from /proc/mounts reach only syscall.Statfs, which is read-only and limited to the realFS block-backed types; network and FUSE filesystems are excluded to avoid hangs. Free-text fields are sanitized. Temps are capped at 16, and parsers are linear with no regex. The parsers use bounds-checked indexing with length guards (len(f)<5, <16, <10), so a malformed procfs line cannot panic. Unsigned arithmetic is guarded (avail>total clamped, delta handles wraps).

local_checks.invariant: The sampler cache and ring buffer must stay bounded and independent of request volume

local_checks.invariant: The Podman socket peer must be a trusted local endpoint: validSocket and candidates() must restrict which path is dialed and who owns it
local_checks.result: validSocket (podman.go:214-224) Lstat-checks that the path is a real socket owned by root or the euid, with no symlink following. Candidates come only from the operator-set -podman-socket flag, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (must be absolute) or the per-uid /run path. All of those are operator-controlled or in directories owned by the same user. A lower-trust local user cannot plant a socket at these paths. The Lstat-to-dial TOCTOU window requires write access to the same user's runtime directory, which is the same authority. Requests are GET only, with fixed paths and validated 64-hex IDs (runningIDs, validID), so no caller-supplied selectors reach the socket. Result is a hardening note only, with no boundary crossing.

local_checks.invariant: Podman-supplied strings (names, image, status, pod, ports, host_ip, protocol) must be bounded and neutralized before reaching the cached snapshot and JSON output, and the CLI fallback must take no injected data
local_checks.result: toContainer and formatPort pass every free-text field through sanitize (util.go:54-72). sanitize makes the text valid UTF-8, replaces control characters, drops Cf format and bidi characters, and caps the rune count. Fields are length-capped (id 12, name 128, image 200, state 24, status 64, pod 128, port strings 64). Ports are capped at 16 per container and containers at 200. Numeric fields are typed numbers. Oversized or overflowing values (a huge Range or Created) do not panic and are only cosmetic. Output is JSON-encoded and rendered via textContent per the architecture, so there is no injection path. viaCLI (podman.go:351-368) uses a fixed argv, a filtered env, Dir=/ and a size-limited stdout buffer, so no request data reaches it. Responses are capped at 8 MiB (getJSON, limitedBuffer). Non-200 bodies are discarded after at most 4 KiB.

local_checks.invariant: Request volume must not amplify Podman work, and a single unauthenticated peer must not trigger refreshes
local_checks.result: A single run goroutine (main.go:165) performs all refreshes. Snapshot() (podman.go:182) is called only from the /api/state handler (server.go:340), which sits behind auth. It stores lastAccess and does a non-blocking send on the 1-buffered wake channel. At most one refresh is therefore pending or running regardless of request rate, and refreshes are serialized. The ticker refreshes only while a caller has been seen in the last 60 s. A stale snapshot triggers at most one extra refresh per cycle. A Podman failure is retried at most every 5 s, or once per wake, with no unbounded retry, and the log is written only when the error message changes. Unauthenticated peers cannot reach Snapshot, so they cannot keep polling alive.

local_checks.invariant: A slow or hostile Podman peer must not wedge the refresh loop, leak resources, or leave a torn or poisoned snapshot
local_checks.result: refresh wraps its work in a 25 s context timeout. The socket client sets ResponseHeaderTimeout to 15 s and DisableKeepAlives, and its idle connections are closed on return. Body reads are bounded to 8 MiB under that context. CLI execution uses exec.CommandContext with WaitDelay=2s, so a hung child is killed. A malformed JSON response returns an error and falls back to the CLI, or stores an error snapshot, and the next tick retries. This is not a persistent poison-record loop, since the failure is not sticky and the data is re-fetched each cycle. store() replaces the whole snapshot under the mutex, and readers copy the struct by value. The Containers slice is never mutated after publication, so there is no torn read. The error snapshot has a nonzero UpdatedAt and Available=false, so stale data is not served as live data. A stats failure degrades to no stats only. Result: no chain from a container-controlled string or response to availability or a trust-boundary effect.

local_checks.invariant: Pre-auth work per request is bounded and cannot retain a shared slot past a deadline
local_checks.result: Pre-auth cost is one SHA-256 pair over at most 16 KiB of header (MaxHeaderBytes), a mutex-guarded map lookup, and a 401. ReadHeaderTimeout 5s, ReadTimeout 10s, WriteTimeout 15s and IdleTimeout 60s bound how long the semaphore slot (64) can be held. The slot is taken only after headers are parsed, so slowloris connections do not consume it. There are no bodies, decompression, upstream calls or per-request allocations that grow.

local_checks.invariant: failLimiter memory and cardinality are bounded, and accounting cannot be cheaply escaped or abused
local_checks.result: The map is capped at authMaxKeys (4096). purge() is O(cap) and runs only when a new key is inserted while full. Keys are IPv4 strings or IPv6 /64 prefixes. Failures are counted only when an Authorization header is present. Success resets the key. The residual issues are hardening only (see the hardening list): lockout evicted under key churn, and shared-key lockout behind a reverse proxy.

hardening: server.go failLimiter keys on RemoteAddr only. If podmon is run behind a reverse proxy (README suggests -allowed-hosts for that case), every client shares the proxy address, so five bad guesses from anyone lock out the legitimate user for five minutes (the lockout check precedes credential verification). Consider documenting it, or an optional trusted-proxy flag.

server.go failLimiter.purge deletes arbitrary entries, including actively locked-out keys, once 4096 keys are held. An attacker with many source keys (for example many IPv6 /64 prefixes) can evict lockouts. The practical gain is small because a 12+ character password is required and each key gets only 5 tries per window.

server.go limit() only bounds in-flight handlers (64) and not accepted TCP connections. There is no cap on connections or per-IP connections. With MemoryMax=96M in the unit, a very large number of idle connections could OOM the process (restarted after 5s). This is plain volumetric exposure on a LAN service and needs sustained volume, so it is not reported as a finding.
server.go: the shared 64-slot semaphore sits after hostCheck but before auth, so an unauthenticated flood can return 503 to the legitimate user. Handlers are cheap, so this is volumetric only.

It sets no style attribute through setAttribute or markup. The header values are constants, with no request-derived data, so no header injection is possible. The app is read-only with no state-changing action, so framing is only a hardening matter, and frame-ancestors and DENY are set anyway. No CORS headers are emitted and CORP is same-origin, so there is no credentialed cross-origin read path.

local_checks.invariant: Static file serving uses an exact map lookup with no path construction, and unexpected asset types or private-response caching cannot occur
local_checks.result: loadStatic walks the embed.FS rooted via fs.Sub(web) in main.go, and the map is keyed by '/'+path. serveStatic does a[r.URL.Path] with no filesystem path built, so no traversal, no directory listing and no suffix-based cache deception. Unknown extensions fail startup. Content-Type comes from a fixed extension table and nosniff is set. Static responses use Cache-Control no-cache with ServeContent validators, and they sit behind authed. The assets are public source and carry no secrets. The embedded fonts and style.css reference only same-origin /fonts/ URLs, and the files in web/ are the only embedded ones (index.html, app.js, style.css, favicon.svg, three woff2 files). API JSON responses carry no-store. Public-cache directives are absent, so there is no cache-deception condition within source.

assignment_rationale: priority: unauthenticated/lowest-trust surfaces first, then credentials/deployment, then lower-trust data ingestion, then browser-side
hardening: server.go securityHeaders does not set Cache-Control: no-store on authenticated static assets (they get no-cache, which still revalidates). Low value because the assets are public source.
server.go securityHeaders sets Strict-Transport-Security only when -tls-cert is set. Deployments behind a TLS-terminating proxy have to add it there (deployment fact outside source).
bookkeeping_note: unit-level reviewed_paths set to the union of check paths; unowned claimed paths dropped: ["web/app.js"]
